tooltip.tieredpower.desc.isotope_separat: Makes fusion fuel from water: it pulls the heavy hydrogen (deuterium) out, 50 mB of water for every 1 mB of deuterium gas, 2 mB each tick. Feed it water from a Sink, Pump or pipes and pipe the deuterium to your Fusion Reactor - or put it right next to one. Speed Upgrades make it faster. Takes power through the bottom.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.tritium_breeder: Breeds tritium, the other fusion fuel, from lithium - using the neutrons of a running Fission Reactor. Place it against a single-block Fission Reactor or a multiblock's Fission Controller and give it lithium ingots: each one becomes 250 mB of tritium gas (one fusion fuel pair) in 20 seconds while the reactor is running. It needs no power of its own. Pipe the tritium to your Fusion Reactor.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.air_separator: Splits air into nitrogen and oxygen with nothing but power - no water, no fuel. Each tick it makes 16 mB of nitrogen and 4 mB of oxygen (about the real mix of air) and pushes both into Gas Pipes. It needs at least one side open to the air. Nitrogen feeds Cryo Injectors; oxygen boosts Gas Burner Generators.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.cryo_injector: Nitrogen cooling for fission. Place it against a Fission Reactor or a Fission Controller and pipe nitrogen in from an Air Separator: while it feeds 20 mB of nitrogen per tick, the reactor makes 50% more power. It only uses nitrogen while the reactor is running.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.reactor_gauge: A screen for your fission reactor. On a multiblock reactor, build it straight into the wall in place of any Fission Casing or Glass block (not edges or corners) - the controller links it when the reactor forms, so it works anywhere on the walls. On a single-block Fission Reactor, just place it against the reactor. Its face shows the heat (green, orange near the limit, red when hot), the power it's making, whether it's running, idle or SCRAMmed, and any add-ons fitted (Neutron Reflector, nitrogen cooling). A comparator next to it reads the heat from 0 to 15 - wire it to the reactor's redstone setting and it can throttle itself before it overheats. It works on Fusion Reactors too: there it shows the plasma temperature, output and plasma tier, and can be built into the fusion multiblock's wall in the same way.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.neutron_reflect: Bounces stray neutrons back into the core, so fuel rods last 50% longer. Right-click a Fission Reactor or Fission Controller to fit one; it shows in Jade and on a Reactor Gauge, and drops back out if the reactor is broken.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.plasma_coil_mk1: Upgrades a Fusion Reactor's plasma. Right-click a Fusion Reactor or a multiblock's Fusion Controller with Mk I, then Mk II, then Mk III (in that order). Mk I doubles the reactor's output, Mk II triples it and Mk III quadruples it. Fuel burns faster too (x1.5, x2, x2.5), but always less than the output gain - so every tier gets more power out of each deuterium + tritium pair. At the higher tiers, pipe the fuel in as gas (Isotope Separator and Tritium Breeder) so it keeps up. Jade and a Reactor Gauge show the tier; the coils drop back out if the reactor is broken.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.particle_collid: Makes antimatter for the Antimatter Reactor by smashing fusion fuel together at enormous energies. Each operation turns 10 mB of deuterium + 10 mB of tritium + 20,000 FE into 1 mB of antimatter - one a tick, more with Speed Upgrades. Pipe deuterium (Isotope Separator) and tritium (Tritium Breeder) in with Gas Pipes and feed it power from below (Quantum Cable is ideal); it pushes antimatter out into Gas Pipes, or straight into an Antimatter Reactor next to it.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.antimatter_reac: The end-game power source. It annihilates antimatter for 50,000 FE per mB - 2.5 times what the Particle Collider spent making it - burning up to 20 mB a tick for up to 1,000,000 FE/t. It holds 50 million FE, pushes power out of every side, and idles (burning nothing) while its buffer is full. Pipe antimatter in from a Particle Collider, or place the two side by side. Its core glows and pulses while it burns.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.cryogenic_conde: The first step of rocket fuel: chills a gas into a liquid using nitrogen as the coolant. Pipe in methane (from a Bio-Digester) or oxygen (from an Air Separator or electrolyzer) plus nitrogen (Air Separator): each operation turns 40 mB of gas + 4 mB of nitrogen + 200 FE into 20 mB of Liquid Methane or Liquid Oxygen. It works on one gas at a time - use a Fluid Filter on its pipe, or one condenser per gas. The liquid comes out into ordinary Fluid Pipes (liquids don't go in Gas Pipes).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.fuel_refinery: Blends methalox Rocket Fuel - the same mix real rockets burn: 10 mB Liquid Methane + 20 mB Liquid Oxygen + 100 FE = 30 mB Rocket Fuel, every tick (faster with Speed Upgrades). A Rocket needs 16,000 mB, which takes about 5,300 mB of Liquid Methane and 10,700 mB of Liquid Oxygen - roughly 135 crops' worth of methane through a Bio-Digester.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.rocket: The rocket for the satellite program, put together from parts made in your existing machines: Hull Plates pressed in a Compressor (4 steel plates each), a Rocket Engine upgraded from a Rocket Nozzle in a Smithing Press (netherite upgrade template + Quantum Alloy), Fuel Tank Sections (Hull Plates around a Quantum Fluid Tank), a Guidance Computer (Storage Terminals and a Molecular Assembler) and a Nose Cone. It needs 16,000 mB of Rocket Fuel and a payload such as a Solar Satellite. Launch it from a Launch Controller and Launch Pad.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.solar_satellite: A Rocket payload: Quantum Solar Panels, superconductor and a Quantum Power Core. Once in orbit it will beam steady power - day and night, in any weather - down to a Receiver Dish - right-click a dish to claim it.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.launch_controll: The brain of a launch site. Build a 3x3 square of Launch Pads (steel deck plates with hazard stripes), put at least one Launch Tower (a steel lattice) right beside the pad, and place the Launch Controller (a desk console) touching the pad. Open the controller: put a Rocket in the top slot - it appears standing on the middle of the pad - and a Solar Satellite in the payload slot, then pipe 16,000 mB of Rocket Fuel into the controller. A checklist shows what's still missing (launch site, rocket, payload, fuel, clear sky). Press LAUNCH: a 10 second countdown appears for everyone nearby, then the rocket lifts off in fire and smoke and climbs out of sight - and a moment later the satellite reaches orbit (the whole server is told). The screen also shows how many satellites are in orbit and how many are linked to dishes. You can also right-click the controller with buckets of Rocket Fuel (16 fill a rocket) - handy in creative for testing.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.launch_pad: A steel deck plate with hazard stripes. Nine of them in a 3x3 make the pad for a Launch Controller; the rocket stands on the middle one. They're only 4 pixels high.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.launch_tower: An open steel lattice tower section. Put at least one beside the Launch Pad - stack more for a proper gantry.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.receiver_dish: Collects the power a Solar Satellite in orbit beams down: about 100,000 FE/t, day and night, in any weather - no fuel, ever. Right-click it to claim one of your satellites that isn't already linked to a dish; sneak + right-click to release it again. It holds 10 million FE and pushes power out of every side. Launch more satellites and build more dishes for more power. Jade shows its satellite and output.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.laser_drill: The Orbital Mining Laser. Build a Mining Satellite (Quantum Solar Panels, superconductor, a Diamond Laser Lens and a Quantum Power Core) and launch it from a Launch Pad like a Solar Satellite. Then place a Laser Drill under open sky: it automatically claims one of your free Mining Satellites, and while it has power the satellite fires a laser beam down from orbit onto the drill - you can see it from far away - and drills out one ore every second (2,000,000 FE each, about 100,000 FE/t: one Solar Satellite and Receiver Dish can run one drill). The ores come from the forge:ores tag, so other mods' ores turn up too; common ores are common and diamonds, emeralds and uranium are rare. Put Laser Lenses (iron, copper, gold, redstone, diamond, uranium) in its input slots to make that ore ten times as likely - several lenses stack. Ores go into its output grid and then into chests, pipes or buses next to it. Item Filters work in its input slots too: set one to Block and the drill never makes those ores - in Name mode one deepslate ore blocks every deepslate_... ore.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.oxygen_furnace: Oxygen-blown steelmaking - how real steelworks do it: oxygen is blown through iron to burn off the carbon. 1 iron ingot (or iron dust) + 100 mB of oxygen = 1 steel ingot in 3 seconds, using 80 FE/t and no coal - much faster than blasting, and cheaper than the Alloy Smelter route. Pipe oxygen in from an Air Separator or Gas Electrolyzer. Speed Upgrades make it faster. Takes Tier Installers: 3, 5, 7, 9 or 12 at once (Advanced to Naquadah).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.bio_digester: Turns farm waste into fuel. Crops, seeds, saplings, leaves, flowers, rotten flesh, kelp, cactus and other plant or animal matter rot down into methane (biogas): 200 mB per item (a Sporecap from the Mycelia planet gives 2,000 mB), one every 2 seconds, with no power needed. Pipe the methane to a Gas Burner Generator, where it's worth 12 FE per mB (15 with oxygen) - a cheap early way into gas power, and a use for all that spare seed and sapling clutter.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.smithing_press: A powered smithing table, so autocrafting can do smithing: netherite upgrades, armour trims and other mods' smithing recipes, 5 seconds each at 60 FE/t. It has a slot each for the template, the item to upgrade and the material, and only takes an item into the slot a recipe uses it in - so pipes and Molecular Assemblers can feed it. For autocrafting, make a processing pattern from the smithing recipe (JEI's + on the vanilla smithing recipe works) and give it to an assembler touching the press. Speed Upgrades make it faster. Takes Tier Installers: 3, 5, 7, 9 or 12 at once (Advanced to Naquadah).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.brewing_machine: An electric brewing stand built for automation. Put glass bottles - or water bottles or potions - in its three bottle slots and an ingredient (nether wart, sugar, a spider eye...) in the slot above. It fills glass bottles with water from its own 4,000 mB tank (333 mB each - pipe water in, or right-click with a water bucket), then brews all three bottles with one ingredient in 5 seconds at 20 FE/t - no blaze powder needed. It uses the game's brewing recipes, so every vanilla potion works, including splash and lingering, and modded brewing too. Feed bottles and ingredients in from the top or sides; finished potions come out of the bottom. For autocrafting, JEI's + on a brewing recipe makes a pattern for three bottles at once with the Brewing Machine set as its machine.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.fluidic_plenish: The opposite of the Electric Pump: it puts fluid into the world. Pipe a fluid in (or right-click with a bucket) and give it power, and it fills the open space below and around it with source blocks - one every half second, using 1,000 mB and 100 FE each - spreading outwards and downwards up to 32 blocks away, but never above its own level. Fill a moat, flood a hole, or lay down lava for a lava farm. Works with any fluid that can exist as a block (water, lava and modded liquids). Jade shows how many blocks it has placed and when it's finished.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.block_mover: Moves blocks that hold things without emptying them. Right-click a chest, machine, tank or any block with contents: it's picked up - everything inside included - and the Block Mover glows while it holds it. Right-click a surface to put it down again. Great for rearranging a base without unloading every chest. It respects storage network security and won't pick up unbreakable blocks.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.ore_scanner: A handheld scanner: right-click to list every kind of ore within 16 blocks of you, how many there are, and the direction and distance to the nearest of each (for example '7 blocks north-east, 4 down'). Finds other mods' ores too. 5,000 FE per scan from its 1,000,000 FE battery - charge it in a Charger or near a Wireless Charger.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.block_breaker: Breaks the block in front of it once a second, as if mined with a diamond pickaxe, and keeps the drops - 400 FE per block. The drops go into chests, pipes or Import Buses next to it. Set its redstone mode to break only on a signal. Pair it with a Block Placer, or put it in front of a cobblestone generator for endless cobblestone.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.block_placer: Places blocks from its 3 input slots in front of it, twice a second - 100 FE per block. Feed it from a pipe or an Export Bus. Together with a Block Breaker it makes a simple stone or cobblestone farm, or moves blocks along a line.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.tree_farm: A hands-off wood supply. It plants saplings all around itself at its own level - on every other block out to 4 blocks away, so 24 trees each with room to grow - on dirt or grass, and fells grown trees (every connected log and leaf), keeping the logs, sticks and apples. Saplings that drop go straight back into its sapling slots, so a handful keeps it going. Put Fertilizer (or bone meal) in the slot on the left and it grows the saplings itself - even at night or in the dark, where saplings normally won't grow: one Fertilizer is 32 growth steps (about 16 trees), bone meal 8. Next to a storage network it keeps itself topped up with Fertilizer and more of its saplings. 2x2 trees (dark oak, giant spruce) won't grow - use single saplings. 200 FE per job; Speed Upgrades help.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.animal_ranch: Looks after animals on a 9x9 area in front of it. It breeds pairs with feed from its inputs (wheat for cows and sheep, seeds for chickens, carrots for pigs... - up to 24 animals in the area), shears sheep for wool, milks cows into empty buckets, and picks up eggs and feathers. Fence the animals in front of it. 200 FE per job.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.fluid_disk_4k: Stores fluids and gases for the network - water, lava, steam, hydrogen, oxygen and other mods' fluids. Put it in a Drive Bay alongside item disks. Contents stay on the disk when you take it out.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.fluid_disk_256k: A big fluid disk - room for a reactor's worth of steam. Four of them make a 1M disk.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.creative_energy: Creative mode only. Unlimited power: it pushes as much as anything next to it will take every tick, and cables can draw as much as they like. Handy for testing builds.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.creative_storag: Creative mode only. A storage disk with practically unlimited room (still 63 item types).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.creative_fluid_: Creative mode only. A fluid disk with practically unlimited room (still 63 fluid and gas types).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.pattern_encoder: Records recipes onto Blank Patterns. The C/P button switches between two kinds. CRAFTING: lay out a crafting-table recipe by clicking items into the grid (copies only - nothing is used up) or press + on a crafting recipe in JEI; the result shows on the right. With the S button on (Substitutes), the pattern accepts every item the recipe allows in each slot - any planks, any cobblestone. PROCESSING: a machine recipe with amounts - left-click a slot with a stack to set that amount, right-click to add one - up to 3 item outputs on the right, and a row of fluid slots underneath: click them with a bucket or tank to set a fluid or gas in or out (right-click adds another container's worth). JEI's + fills all of it from machine recipes, fluids included. Then put a Blank Pattern in the top-right slot, press Encode and take the pattern from the slot below. In Processing mode the lightning-bolt button fills any energy item in the outputs to full charge - with the same item as the input, that's a charging pattern for a Charger. Crafting patterns don't care about charge: a charged jetpack or battery box in storage is used just like an empty one (enchanted or renamed items never are). Processing mode also has a Machine slot (right of the grid): click it with the machine the recipe runs in. Patterns kept in an Assembly Matrix need it so the network knows which machines to use; JEI's + fills it in for this mod's machines, furnaces and smithing.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.blank_pattern: Encode a recipe onto it in a Pattern Encoder. A Crafting Pattern can be wiped back to blank with sneak + right-click in the air.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.molecular_assem: Does the work for autocrafting: holds up to 9 patterns, plus Speed and Efficiency upgrade slots. Crafting patterns are crafted inside it - one craft every 8 ticks, plus one more per Speed Upgrade (up to 5 at once). Processing patterns are done by the MACHINE TOUCHING the assembler: it sends the item and fluid inputs in and pulls the item, fluid and gas results back into storage, like AE2's Pattern Provider. Tips: the machine's face touching the assembler must be In + Out (the default), and turn the machine's auto-output off so the results wait for the assembler. Built-in smelting: put an assembler against an Electric Furnace and the network knows every furnace recipe without patterns - a missing Iron Ingot is smelted from raw iron, iron ore or iron dust in storage (your own patterns always come first). Machines that use water, like the Ore Purifier, get it from their own Sink or pipe, so water is never 'missing' from a plan.  It works against any face of this mod's machines - the machine's Sides settings don't apply to assemblers - and several assemblers can share one machine. Its glass case shows the crafting core inside, which lights up while it works. Once you build an Assembly Matrix, assemblers (and the simpler Machine Connector) also run the Matrix's patterns on the machines they touch.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.crafting_cpu: Runs crafting jobs - 1 at a time per Basic CPU, 2 Advanced, 4 Elite, 8 Quantum (raise it with Crafting Upgrades); extra requests wait in a queue. Right-click it to see every job and how far along it is; sneak + right-click to cancel them (anything already crafted stays in storage). A network needs at least one CPU and an Assembly Matrix (or Molecular Assembler) to autocraft. When a job is stuck, the Jobs screen says exactly why: the machine it's waiting on (with its position), the ingredient it needs, or that no assembler holds the pattern. In a terminal's Jobs screen, click a job to see each of its steps: how many are left, how many are running, and on which machine.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.matrix_controll: The Assembly Matrix is a central pattern store for your whole network. Build a box from 3x3x3 up to 7x7x7 out of Matrix Casing (Matrix Glass works too, so you can see inside), with one Matrix Controller in a wall. Then swap any wall blocks for Pattern Banks (27 patterns each) and Crafting Accelerators - they can also go inside the box, and empty space inside is fine. Connect any part of it to the storage network with Storage Cable. Right-click the controller to store patterns: each page is one Pattern Bank. Crafting patterns are made inside the Matrix itself - 2 crafts per cycle, plus 2 per Crafting Accelerator. Processing patterns run on ANY machine of the right type that has a Molecular Assembler or a Machine Connector touching it, anywhere on the network - so two furnaces with connectors run your smelting twice as fast without copying a single pattern. Every processing pattern in the Matrix needs its Machine set in the Pattern Encoder (JEI's + does it for this mod's machines). The screen says what's wrong if the box isn't right. The controller's screen also lists every machine the Matrix can use (a panel on the right). Put at least one Pattern Bank inside before storing patterns. To set (or change) which machine a processing pattern uses, click the pattern in the controller's screen while holding that machine's item - hovering a pattern with no machine reminds you.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.pattern_bank: Part of an Assembly Matrix: holds 27 patterns, filled from the Matrix Controller's screen (one bank per page). Put it in place of any wall block, or inside the box. Drops its patterns if broken.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.crafting_accele: Part of an Assembly Matrix: each one adds crafts per cycle for the Matrix's crafting patterns - +2 Basic, +4 Advanced, +8 Elite, +16 Quantum (raise it with Crafting Upgrades, up to 256 per Matrix). Put it in place of any wall block, or inside the box.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.matrix_casing: The frame and walls of an Assembly Matrix. Matrix Glass can replace it in the walls (not needed on edges).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.matrix_glass: See-through wall block for an Assembly Matrix.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.assembler_panel: A flat Molecular Assembler: the same 9 pattern slots, screen, Speed Upgrades and everything else, but as a thin panel stuck onto a machine's face instead of a whole block. Sneak + right-click to place it on a machine (a plain right-click would open the machine), then connect Storage Cable to it. Turn a Molecular Assembler into a panel in the crafting grid, and back again.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.machine_connect: A flat panel that connects a machine to the storage network so the Assembly Matrix can use it - like a Molecular Assembler with no pattern slots and no screen. Sneak + right-click to stick it onto any face of a machine (plain right-click would open the machine), then run Storage Cable to the panel. The Matrix's patterns for that kind of machine run there, 4 operations per cycle (8 Advanced, 16 Elite, 32 Quantum with Crafting Upgrades), and the Matrix Controller's screen lists every connected machine. Early on, use Molecular Assemblers (patterns live in each one); once you have a Matrix, switch to Connectors. On an Electric Furnace it also enables built-in smelting.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.stock_keeper: Keeps items in stock automatically. Click one of its 9 slots with an item to add it (keeps 64 to start); click the slot to select it, type an amount and press Set, or x to remove it. Every 5 seconds, if storage has fewer than the target and nothing is already being made, it starts a crafting job for the difference - so ask it to keep 256 Superconductor Ingots and it quietly tops them up. The bar under each slot: green = in stock, blue = crafting, red = can't craft (missing ingredients or no pattern).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.multimeter: Right-click a cable to see its whole network: power coming in, power going to machines, power going into storage, and how much is stored. Right-click any other block - including other mods' machines and batteries - to see its stored energy, what it's generating right now and what's in its tanks. Machines don't open their screens when you use it, so it's safe to click around. On an item pipe it lists every connection (Push or Pull), what each Pull connection can take out, and whether each Push destination would accept it - the quickest way to find out why items aren't moving. On a machine it also lists each face's setting and what an Out face has ready.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.energy_meter: Goes in a cable line. Power goes in the LEFT side and out the RIGHT side as you look at its screen (the top shows an arrow). The screen shows FE per tick and a running total; right-click for the peak as well, sneak + right-click to reset. A redstone signal switches the flow off, so it doubles as a power switch for a whole branch of your base. A comparator next to it gets a stronger signal the more power flows.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.power_monitor: Place it touching any cable and its screen shows that whole cable network: In (generators and discharging batteries), Use (machines), Chg (going into batteries) and how full the batteries are. Right-click for the full readout. A comparator reads how full the batteries are, 0-15: put a comparator and a redstone torch between it and a Coal Generator set to run on redstone, and the generator only burns fuel when your batteries run low. Right-click it to open a history graph: power generated (green), power used (red) and battery fill (blue) over the last 10 minutes or 2 hours - hover the graph for exact values. Sneak + right-click for the quick readout.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.storage_control: The heart of an item storage network. Link Drive Bays and Storage Terminals to it with Storage Cable (or place them touching it). Power it with a normal energy cable. Only one controller per network - two and the network switches off. It also works as one big inventory: point an Item Pipe into it to store things automatically, or pull items out of it with a pipe or hopper. Right-click it to see its status.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.storage_cable: Links the parts of a storage network together: Storage Controller, Drive Bays and Storage Terminals. It carries no power or items itself - the controller still needs an energy cable.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.drive_bay: Holds 8 Storage Disks. It glows when its network is online. Its screen shows how full the disks inside are.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.disk_workbench: Sets up your disks. Put a Storage or Fluid Disk in, then click items into its 18 partition slots - the disk will then only accept those items (an empty partition takes anything). For a Fluid Disk, click the slots with a bucket or tank of each fluid. Fill partitions the disk to exactly what's already stored on it; Clear removes the partition. Priority runs from -9 to +9: when items are stored, higher-priority disks are filled first, and at the same priority a disk partitioned for the item beats a general one. So make an ores disk at priority +1 and the rest at 0, and ores always land on it. Everything is saved on the disk, so it keeps its setup in any Drive Bay.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.security_termin: Locks a storage network. Place it anywhere on the network: whoever places it becomes the owner, and right-clicking it lets them add or remove trusted players by name (anyone who has joined the server, online or not). Everyone else can't open the network's terminals, Drive Bays, buses, assemblers or Stock Keeper, can't use or link wireless terminals to it, can't break its blocks, and can't place storage parts, pipes or other inventories against it. Only the owner can break the Security Terminal. Server operators can always get in. A network without one stays open to everyone.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.storage_monitor: A screen for your storage. Connect it to the network (touching a Storage Cable or another storage block) and right-click it with any item: its face shows that item and how many the network holds, updating live - green when you have some, red at zero. Right-click with an empty hand to read the exact count; sneak + right-click with an empty hand to clear it. A comparator reads the stock: 0 at none, then one more per doubling (1, 2, 4, 8 ... 16,384+ = 15), so a comparator and a redstone torch make a low-stock alarm - or wire it to a machine to make more when you run low.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.storage_termina: Shows everything stored in the network in one searchable grid. Click to take a stack, right-click to take half, shift-click to send it straight to your inventory. Click the grid while holding an item to store it (right-click stores just one), or shift-click items in your inventory to store them. Fluids and gases show too (amounts in buckets): hold an empty bucket or tank and click a fluid to fill it, or click the grid with a full one to pour it in. Type to search by name, or @modname for one mod. The All / Items / Fluids button picks what to show; 123 / A-Z switches the sort. While the network is crafting, a live crafting queue shows beside the terminal.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.crafting_termin: A Storage Terminal with a 3x3 crafting grid underneath. Craft straight from storage: when a craft uses up a grid slot it refills from storage, so shift-clicking the result crafts as many as your stored materials allow. The x button (or closing the terminal) puts the grid back into storage. With JEI, open any crafting recipe and press + to fill the grid from storage; shift + fills a stack of each. Missing ingredients show in red. Craft All Missing: after JEI's + fills the grid, a + button under the grid starts crafting whatever storage was missing and fills it in as it's made. While the network is crafting, a live crafting queue shows beside the terminal.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.import_bus: Moves things FROM the block it faces INTO storage. Place it against a chest, furnace, machine or tank (it faces the block you click on) and connect it to the network with Storage Cable. It takes items, fluids and gases. Right-click to set a filter; with an empty filter it takes everything. To filter a fluid, click a filter slot with a bucket or tank of it. The screen shows whether it's connected to a powered network.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.export_bus: Moves things FROM storage INTO the block it faces - it never takes anything out of that block. Right-click and set what to send: items, or a bucket/tank for a fluid or gas. With an empty filter it sends nothing. Good for keeping a Pulverizer fed with ore, a Coal Generator topped up with coal, or a Steam Turbine supplied with stored steam.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.storage_termina: A flat Storage Terminal for walls, floors and ceilings, like AE2's. Place it on a Storage Cable or any storage block; the screen faces away from the surface you click. Craft it from a Storage Terminal block, and back again. While the network is crafting, a live crafting queue shows beside the terminal.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.crafting_termin: A flat Crafting Terminal. Works exactly like the block version. Craft it from a Crafting Terminal block (and back), or from a Storage Terminal Panel plus a crafting table. Craft All Missing: after JEI's + fills the grid, a + button under the grid starts crafting whatever storage was missing and fills it in as it's made. While the network is crafting, a live crafting queue shows beside the terminal.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.storage_interfa: A doorway into storage from anywhere on the Storage Cable. Anything next to it - Item Pipes, Fluid and Gas Pipes, machines, reactors, hoppers - can push items, fluids and gases into storage or pull them out, as if it were one huge chest and tank. Put one next to a Fission Reactor to store its steam, and an Export Bus on a Steam Turbine elsewhere to use it.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.wireless_termin: Your storage in your hand. Sneak + right-click a Storage Controller to link it, then right-click anywhere within 64 blocks (in the same dimension) to open a full Storage Terminal - items, fluids, search and all. It runs on FE, using a little while it's open; charge it in a Charger, Wireless Charger or Portable Battery. Set the Open Wireless Terminal key in Controls > Key Binds > Tiered Industries and you can open it straight from your inventory. While the network is crafting, a live crafting queue shows beside the terminal.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.wireless_crafti: A Wireless Terminal with a crafting grid: craft from storage wherever you are, with auto-refill and the JEI + button, just like the Crafting Terminal. Make it from a Wireless Terminal and a crafting table. Craft All Missing: after JEI's + fills the grid, a + button under the grid starts crafting whatever storage was missing and fills it in as it's made. While the network is crafting, a live crafting queue shows beside the terminal.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.wireless_access: Extends your wireless terminals' reach. Put it anywhere on the storage network (touching Storage Cable or another storage block) and Wireless Terminals work within 128 blocks of it, as well as 64 blocks of the controller. Place a few to cover a big base or reach your mining area. The tip glows while the network is online.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.storage_disk_4k: Stores items for the network - put it in a Drive Bay. Everything stays on the disk if you take it out, so you can move a disk to another network. The bar under the disk shows how full it is.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.storage_disk_25: A big disk - enough for a few full chests of every common block. Four of them make a 1M disk.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.guide_book: The in-game version of this guide: categories, search, item pages and live recipes read from your game (so modpack changes show up). Every player gets one the first time they join.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.wrench: Right-click: rotate machines, cycle Battery Box faces, switch Bank Ports, or switch a pipe connection between delivering and pulling. Shift + right-click any Tiered Industries block to pick it up with its items, energy and settings kept.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.speed_upgrade: Makes a machine work faster: +50% speed per card, up to 8 cards (x5). Each one also raises the power use per tick, so pair them with Energy Upgrades. Put them in the machine's Upgrades window - the green arrow button at the top of its screen - or shift-click them in from your inventory.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.efficiency_upgr: The Energy Upgrade (it used to be called Efficiency): each card cuts a machine's power use by 15%, up to 8 cards (about 73% less). Goes in the machine's Upgrades window next to the Speed cards.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.advanced_instal: Upgrades a processing machine in place - right-click it with the installer. Advanced machines run 3 operations side by side on the same progress bar, Elite 5, Ultimate 7 and Quantum 9, using power for each one running. Install the tiers in order (Advanced first). Contents, upgrades and settings are kept, and the installers drop back out if you break the machine. Works on the Electric Furnace, Pulverizer, Alloy Smelter, Compressor, Electric Sawmill, Ore Purifier, Rock Crusher, Fluid Mixer and Chemical Washer. The machine's Upgrades window shows its tier.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.elite_installer: The second machine tier: right-click an Advanced machine to make it Elite (5 operations at once). Made with diamonds.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.ultimate_instal: The third machine tier: right-click an Elite machine to make it Ultimate (7 operations at once). Made with netherite.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.quantum_install: The fifth machine tier: right-click an Ultimate machine to make it Quantum (9 operations at once). Made with Quantum Alloy. The Naquadah Installer (from the Inferno planet) goes one step further.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.muffler: Silences a machine: right-click any machine with it. To take it off, open the machine's Upgrades window and press Remove. It drops back out if the machine is broken.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.quarry_planner: Choose exactly where your Quarry digs. Right-click one corner block, then the block at the opposite corner, then right-click the Quarry: it digs that rectangle (up to 65 x 65), from the higher corner's level down to its depth setting. The area can be anywhere - next to the Quarry or across the valley - as long as its chunks are loaded (a Chunk Loader helps). The Quarry's screen shows the planned size; its Centred/Behind button goes back to the normal modes. Sneak + right-click the air to clear the corners.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.electric_drill: Mines anything a pickaxe or shovel can, at diamond level. Runs on energy instead of durability - charge it in a Charger, Wireless Charger or Portable Battery. With no charge it barely scratches blocks.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.advanced_drill: Netherite-level and faster. Shift + right-click in the air to switch between single-block and 3x3 mining.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.electric_chains: Cuts anything an axe can, plus leaves and cobwebs. Breaking a log fells the whole tree (up to 128 logs); sneak to cut just one.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.jetpack: Wear it in the chest slot and hold jump to fly. Uses energy only while thrusting, and stops fall damage while it has charge. On a dedicated server, set allow-flight=true in server.properties.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.advanced_jetpac: Climbs much faster, holds ten times the energy and gives more protection.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.portable_batter: A battery you carry. Right-click to switch it on (it glows): it then charges every other powered item in your inventory and armour - including other mods' tools.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.advanced_portab: Bigger and much faster Portable Battery.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.wireless_charge: Charges the powered items carried or worn by every player within 16 blocks. Power it with cables like any machine.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.uranium_ore: Found from Y 24 down to the bottom of the world, most common deep down. Glows faintly. Needs an iron pickaxe.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.raw_uranium: Dropped by uranium ore. Smelt it, or pulverize/purify it for more.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.uranium_ingot: Made into Fuel Rods. Other mods' uranium ingots work too.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.uranium_fuel_ro: Fission Reactor fuel. Burns for 5 minutes at up to 800 FE/t.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.depleted_fuel_r: A spent fuel rod. Pulverize it to get a Uranium Dust back.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.mox_fuel_rod: Mixed-oxide fuel - uranium with plutonium bred in your reactors. It works in both Fission Reactors and their Fuel Ports, alongside or instead of uranium rods. Each MOX rod lasts twice as long and gives 50% more power, but also 50% more heat, so make sure your cooling keeps up (a Cryo Injector helps). The multiblock burns its MOX rods first. MOX depletes into a normal Depleted Fuel Rod, so the cycle keeps going as long as you add uranium. Made from steel, 2 uranium ingots and 1 plutonium ingot (makes 2).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.plutonium_ingot: The second nuclear fuel. Reprocess Depleted Fuel Rods in a Chemical Washer with chlorine and water - each rod gives 1 Plutonium Dust - then smelt the dust into ingots. Used to make MOX Fuel Rods. (If you'd rather get uranium back, the Pulverizer turns a depleted rod into uranium dust instead.)
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.steel_ingot: Used in most mid-game recipes. Make it in a blast furnace from iron, or faster in the Alloy Smelter from iron and coal.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.lithium_ore: Found below Y=0. Needs an iron pickaxe; Fortune and Silk Touch work.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.deepslate_lithi: The deepslate version - most lithium is found in deepslate.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.raw_lithium: Dropped by lithium ore. Smelt it, or pulverize/purify it for more.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.lithium_ingot: Needed for Tritium Cells and Superconductor.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.superconductor_: Made in the Alloy Smelter from copper and lithium. Used for Magnet Coils, Speed Upgrades and top-tier recipes.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.quantum_alloy_i: The Tier 5 material. Made in the Alloy Smelter from 1 netherite ingot and 4 Superconductor Ingots (makes 2). Used for every Quantum block.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.iron_plate: Made in the Compressor. Works with other mods that use plates.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.sawdust: By-product of the Electric Sawmill. Burns as fuel, and 4 compress into paper.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.empty_fuel_cell: Filled in the Electrolyzer. Fusion reactors hand the empty cells back.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.deuterium_cell: Fusion fuel, made from water in the Electrolyzer.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.tritium_cell: Fusion fuel, made from lithium in the Electrolyzer.
jei.tieredpower.info.energy_core: The Energy Core stores huge amounts of power: 20 billion FE at tier I, 100 billion at II, 1 trillion at III, 10 trillion at IV and 100 trillion at tier V (Core Upgrades, applied in order by right-clicking the core). Place Input Pylons (feed them with cables) and Output Pylons (they push into anything touching them) within 8 blocks - they link to the nearest core by themselves; each moves 1M FE/t at tier I up to 256M FE/t at tier V. The orb inside grows and brightens as it fills. It keeps its energy when broken, and a comparator reads how full it is.
jei.tieredpower.info.logic_controller: Simple rules for a smart base. Connect it to your storage network and open it: each of its 4 rules says IF something THEN give a redstone signal out of a side. Item: how many of an item the network holds is below or above a number (click the item into the rule's slot). Power: how full the batteries touching the controller are, in percent. Redstone: the controller is receiving a signal. A side any true rule points at gives a full-strength signal - set the machines next to it to run on a redstone signal.
config.jade.plugin_tieredpower.crafting_: Tiered Industries crafting CPU and accelerator tiers
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.crafting_upgrad: Right-click a Crafting CPU, Crafting Accelerator or Machine Connector of the tier below to make it Advanced. Tiers go in order: Basic, Advanced, Elite, Quantum. The block keeps its tier when broken, and its light strip shows the tier.

Right-click a Crafting CPU, Crafting Accelerator or Machine Connector of the tier below to make it Elite. Tiers go in order: Basic, Advanced, Elite, Quantum. The block keeps its tier when broken, and its light strip shows the tier.

Right-click a Crafting CPU, Crafting Accelerator or Machine Connector of the tier below to make it Quantum. Tiers go in order: Basic, Advanced, Elite, Quantum. The block keeps its tier when broken, and its light strip shows the tier.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.conveyor_belt: Carries dropped items along in the direction it faces (away from you when placed) - you can watch everything move. Mobs and players ride it too (sneak to stand still). At the end of a belt, items go into any chest, machine or pipe in front of it; hoppers, pipes and Export Buses can put items onto a belt. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand to make it a slope that goes up a block, then down a block, then flat again. Items on belts don't despawn.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.fast_conveyor_b: A Conveyor Belt at twice the speed: 2.5 blocks per second. Works the same way - slopes with sneak + right-click.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.express_conveyo: The fastest belt: 5 blocks per second. Works the same way - slopes with sneak + right-click.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.belt_splitter: Items reaching the middle go out left, straight on and right in turn - only to sides with a belt or an inventory. Use it to feed a row of machines from one belt. Runs at Express speed so it never holds a belt back.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.filter_belt: Items in its filter turn off to the left (sneak + right-click with an empty hand to switch to the right); everything else goes straight on. Right-click with an item to add it to the filter, again to take it out (up to 9 items); right-click with an empty hand to see the filter. Runs at Express speed.
jei.tieredpower.info.conveyor_belt: Moves dropped items, mobs and players. Basic 1.25 blocks/s, Fast 2.5, Express 5. Delivers into whatever inventory is at its end. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand: slope up / slope down / flat.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.drone_station: Launches up to 4 Utility Drones and gives them work. Click the mode button: Harvest picks ripe crops within 12 blocks and replants them; Collect picks up dropped items within 12 blocks; Fetch brings items here from a linked inventory; Deliver takes items from here to a linked inventory (link one with a Drone Remote, up to 64 blocks away). Whatever the drones bring back goes into the station's 15 slots, which pipes, hoppers, belts and buses can empty. Uses 20 FE/t for each drone out working. Redstone control pauses it and calls the drones home.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.utility_drone: Put it in a Drone Station's drone slots and it flies out to work - harvesting, collecting, fetching or delivering, depending on the station's mode. Drones fly through anything and can't be hurt.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.drone_remote: Links a Drone Station to an inventory for Fetch and Deliver: right-click the chest (or machine), then right-click the station. Sneak + right-click a station to clear its link.
jei.tieredpower.info.drone_station: Up to 4 Utility Drones. Modes: Harvest (ripe crops within 12 blocks, replanted), Collect (dropped items within 12 blocks), Fetch and Deliver (to or from an inventory linked with a Drone Remote, up to 64 blocks away). Results go into the station's 15 slots. 20 FE/t per working drone.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.turbine_control: The brain of the Industrial Turbine, a multiblock steam turbine that grows with its size. Build a hollow box from 3x3x3 up to 13x13x13: Turbine Casing on the edges and corners; Casing, Turbine Glass and Turbine Valves on the walls, with this controller in one wall; Turbine Rotors (and air) inside. Pipe steam into a valve. Each rotor passes 200 mB/t of steam, and more rotors make each mB worth more: x1.3 with one rotor up to x2 with 15 or more; up to 128 rotors count (at the default 2 FE per mB, that's up to 4 FE per mB). The steam condenses back into water (1 mB per 10 mB of steam), which the valves push out, so you can pipe it back to your boilers. Right-click the controller to see what's missing if it won't form.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.turbine_casing: Frame and walls of the Industrial Turbine. Edges and corners must be casing.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.turbine_glass: See-through wall for the Industrial Turbine, to watch the blades spin.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.turbine_valve: Goes in an Industrial Turbine wall: takes steam in, and pushes power and condensed water out into whatever touches it. Cables and pipes can also pull from it.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.turbine_rotor: A shaft section for the inside of an Industrial Turbine. Each one lets 200 mB/t of steam through and raises the turbine's efficiency. Its blades appear and spin once the turbine forms.
jei.tieredpower.info.turbine_controller: Industrial Turbine: hollow box 3x3x3 to 13x13x13. Edges: Turbine Casing. Walls: Casing, Glass, Valves and this controller. Inside: Turbine Rotors and air. 200 mB/t steam per rotor, efficiency x1.3 (1 rotor) to x2 (15+). Holds 2,000 mB of steam per inside block. Condenses 1 mB water per 10 mB steam.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.spatial_project: Picks up a whole cube of blocks and puts it down somewhere else. Insert a Spatial Cell and a cube outline appears on top of the projector, centred over it (3, 7 or 15 wide, by the cell). Press Capture: every block in the cube - chests and machines with everything in them - goes into the cell and leaves air. Carry the cell to another projector (or move this one), make sure the outlined area is empty, and press Deploy to put it all back exactly as it was. Costs 40 FE per block moved. Can't capture unbreakable blocks like bedrock.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.spatial_cell_sm: Holds one captured 3x3x3 space for a Spatial Projector. Shimmers while full.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.spatial_cell_me: Holds one captured 7x7x7 space for a Spatial Projector - a small machine room.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.spatial_cell_la: Holds one captured 15x15x15 space for a Spatial Projector - a whole base wing.
jei.tieredpower.info.spatial_projector: Insert a Spatial Cell (3, 7 or 15 wide): Capture takes every block in the outlined cube above the projector (with contents) into the cell; Deploy puts it back into an empty area. 40 FE per block. Unbreakable blocks can't be captured.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.overclock_accel: A Quantum-tier Assembly Matrix part. It adds 16 crafts per cycle like a Quantum Crafting Accelerator, and while the Matrix is running jobs, every machine it crafts with (through Machine Connectors, buses and assemblers) runs as if it had 2 more Speed upgrades - up to 8 more from 4 Overclock Accelerators. Overclocked machines use more power, just like with Speed upgrades. Made from a Quantum Crafting Accelerator.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.item_magnet: Pulls dropped items and XP orbs to you from 6 blocks away while it's on. Sneak + right-click to switch it on or off. Works from your hotbar, needs no power. Items on conveyor belts and near a collecting Drone Station are left alone; sneak to stop pulling for a moment.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.advanced_item_m: Reaches 12 blocks and works from anywhere in your inventory. Runs on FE (charge it in a Charger; a little power per item pulled). Ignore list: hold an item in your off hand and right-click with the magnet to stop pulling it (again to remove it, up to 9 items). Sneak + right-click to switch on or off.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.fluid_disk_1m: Holds 1,048,576 buckets of fluids and gases - four 256K disks in one. Made from 4 Fluid Storage Disks (256K), superconductor and a nether star.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.fluid_disk_4m: Holds 4,194,304 buckets of fluids and gases: an endgame tank for steam, deuterium, oxygen or rocket fuel in a single drive bay slot. Made from 4 Fluid Storage Disks (1M), Quantum Alloy and a Quantum Power Core.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.storage_disk_1m: Holds 1,048,576 items - four 256K disks in one. Made from 4 Storage Disks (256K), superconductor and a nether star.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.storage_disk_4m: Holds 4,194,304 items in one drive bay slot. Made from 4 Storage Disks (1M), Quantum Alloy and a Quantum Power Core.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.elevator: Put elevators above each other in a shaft (up to 32 blocks apart, with two blocks of room above each). Stand on one and jump to go up to the next, or sneak to go down. Right-click with a dye to colour it: elevators only take you to their own colour, so several lifts can share a shaft. Needs no power.
jei.tieredpower.info.elevator: Stand on an Elevator and jump to go to the next one above, or sneak to go down - up to 32 blocks, same colour only. Colour it by right-clicking with a dye. No power needed.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.stargate_frame: Build a standing 7x7 square of these (24 blocks, empty inside, facing either way), then right-click any of them with an empty hand: the square turns into a round Stargate like the one on TV - a thick ring with a recessed band of glyphs and nine chevrons. When you dial, the glyph band spins and the chevrons lock one by one before the vortex bursts out of the gate and settles into the rippling event horizon. Don't stand in front of it. Breaking any piece turns it back into blocks. Put a Stargate Dialler within 8 blocks.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.stargate_dialer: A DHD (Dial Home Device), like on TV: a pedestal with a sloping keypad. Right-click it for the keypad - two rings of glyph keys around a big red dome. Press the six glyphs of an address, then the point of origin (the pyramid), then the dome; the Addresses list types one in for you. A formed (round) gate spins up and locks its chevrons, then the vortex bursts out (anything in front of the gate is vaporised - players are only thrown clear) and the event horizon stays open for 30 seconds - walk through to travel. The gate at the other end lights up too. Press the dome (or Close gate) to shut it early. Redstone: pick an address at the bottom of the keypad, and a redstone signal into the DHD dials it and holds the gate open until the signal goes off. From home every gate costs 50 billion FE to dial plus 1 million FE/t while open, so feed it from an Energy Core (Output Pylons) or a big bank of cables; it holds 100 billion. Each planet is a whole world that generates as you explore. Frost, Dune, Verdant, Inferno, Abyss, Skylands, Mycelia and Crystal Depths are in the address list from the start; eight hidden worlds (Eden, Karoo, Redwood, Murk, Titan, Wraith, Umbra and Void Reach) need their address found first - see Stargate Address. The first visit builds a landing platform with its own gate and DHD, and dialling from a planet is free - Home takes you back to where you left, or go on to another planet. Close gate (or the dome) also shuts an incoming connection opened by the DHD at the other end; dialling a world that's already connected just tells you to walk through.
jei.tieredpower.info.stargate_dialer: Stargate: build a standing 7x7 ring of Stargate Frame (empty inside) and put a DHD (Dialler) within 8 blocks. Dialling from home costs 50 billion FE plus 1 million FE/t while open; from a planet it's free. Known from the start: Frost, Dune, Verdant, Inferno, Abyss, Skylands, Mycelia, Crystal Depths. Hidden (find a Stargate Address): Eden, Karoo, Redwood, Murk, Titan, Wraith, Umbra, Void Reach. Each landing platform has a free return gate and a supply chest.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.quantum_chest: A 54-slot chest that moves items between worlds at a quantum level - no Stargate needed. Every Quantum Chest starts as a main chest: put one at your base. Link others to it with a Quantum Linker - from any distance and any world, as many as you like. A linked chest has a Send / Receive button at the top of its window. Send (the default): anything that goes into it (by hand, hopper, pipe or machine) appears in the main chest about twice a second; set items in its filter row to send only those and keep the rest. Receive: the main chest sends it the items on its filter row - e.g. food, fuel and torches out to a planet base (it needs at least one filter item). The main chest's window shows how many chests are linked to it, sending and receiving. If the chest at the other end isn't loaded, items wait in transit (up to 270 stacks for a main chest, 54 for a Receive chest) and arrive when it loads; a chest only sends while its own area is loaded (you nearby, or a Chunk Loader). Pipes and the storage network work with it like any chest. Breaking a chest drops its contents plus anything in transit to it. Crafts in pairs.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.quantum_linker: Links Quantum Chests. Sneak + right-click your main Quantum Chest to record it (the linker glows), then right-click any number of other Quantum Chests to link them - in this world or another. The linker keeps the main chest, so one trip can link chests on several planets. Sneak + right-click a linked chest to unlink it (it becomes a main chest again).
jei.tieredpower.info.quantum_chest: Quantum Chests: each one starts as a main chest. Sneak + right-click your main chest with a Quantum Linker, then right-click other Quantum Chests to link them - any distance, any world. A linked chest is Send (its items go to the main chest; a filter limits which) or Receive (the main chest sends it the items on its filter). Items wait in transit while the other end isn't loaded.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.cryonite_ore: Found only on the Frost planet, in ice, snow and stone. Drops 2-4 Cryonite Shards (more with Fortune).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.cryonite_shard: Glowing ice crystal from the Frost planet. Nine make a Block of Cryonite; also used in the Aether Stabilizer Module.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.cryonite_block: Put it inside a multiblock Fission Reactor: it counts as three Coolant Channels.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.solarite_sand: Golden, faintly glowing sand found only on the Dune planet. Smelt it into Solar Glass.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.solar_glass: Glowing golden glass made from Solarite Sand. The top of the Stellar Solar Panel.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.livingwood_log: Wood from the Livingwood trees that grow only on the Verdant planet. Craft one with 4 bone meal for 16 Fertilizer, or into planks.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.livingwood_plan: Planks from Livingwood - green, for building.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.naquadah_ore: The rare metal of the Inferno planet, in netherrack, basalt and blackstone. Needs a diamond pickaxe. Drops Raw Naquadah; doubles in the Pulverizer, triples in the Ore Purifier like any ore.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.raw_naquadah: Smelt into Naquadah Ingots, or process it for more.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.naquadah_ingot: The planet metal: makes the Naquadah Installer (a sixth machine tier), Mk II upgrades, the Stellar Solar Panel and cheap Stargate Frames (8 from 4 ingots and 4 steel plates).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.abyssal_pearl_o: Found only on the Abyss planet, in the stone and sand of the sea bed. Drops Abyssal Pearls.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.abyssal_pearl: Right-click to crush it: 10 minutes of water breathing, night vision and dolphin's grace - made for exploring the Abyss.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.aether_crystal_: Found only on the Skylands planet, in the stone of the floating islands. Drops Aether Crystals.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.aether_crystal: A light, pink crystal that seems to want to float. The key to the Aether Stabilizer Module.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.sporecap: A glowing mushroom that grows only on the Mycelia planet. In a Bio-Digester one Sporecap makes 2,000 mB of methane - ten times ordinary biomass.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.resonance_cryst: Found only in the Crystal Depths, in stone, calcite, tuff and dripstone. Needs a diamond pickaxe. Drops Resonance Crystals.
A humming blue crystal. Makes the Mk II Speed and Energy upgrades and the Naquadah Installer.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.speed_upgrade_2: Goes in a machine's Speed slot and counts as two Speed upgrades - so a full stack of 8 gives 16 (x9 speed). Made from Speed Upgrades, Resonance Crystals and a Naquadah Ingot.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.efficiency_upgr: Goes in a machine's Energy slot and counts as two Energy upgrades - a full stack of 8 gives 16 (about -85% power, the most any machine can save). Made from Energy Upgrades, Resonance Crystals and a Naquadah Ingot.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.naquadah_instal: The sixth machine tier: right-click a Quantum machine to make it Naquadah (12 operations at once). A Chunk Loader at Naquadah tier reaches 19x19 chunks.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.stellar_solar_p: Tier 6 solar: 36,000 FE/t in full sun - four times a Quantum Solar Panel. Solar Glass over four Quantum Solar Panels, a Naquadah Ingot and Quantum Cable.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.aether_stabiliz: A Quantum Suit chestplate module: Flight uses a quarter of the power (25 FE/t). Made from a Flight Module, Aether Crystals and Cryonite Shards.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.address_tablet: An old stone tablet carved with the six glyphs of a hidden world. Eight more worlds lie beyond the first eight - Eden, Karoo, Redwood, Murk, Titan, Wraith, Umbra and Void Reach - but their addresses have to be found. Tablets turn up in chests all over: desert and jungle temples, strongholds, ancient cities, shipwrecks, buried treasure, mansions, bastions, end cities, dungeons, mineshafts, outposts and more - and every planet's landing platform has a supply chest with the address of another hidden world. Right-click to learn it: it joins your DHD's address list. You can also just type its glyphs on the DHD (shown on the tablet); dialling a world teaches you its address too. The tablet isn't used up, so pass it to a friend.
jei.tieredpower.info.address_tablet: Not crafted: found in chests (temples, strongholds, ancient cities, shipwrecks, buried treasure, mansions, bastions, end cities, dungeons, mineshafts, outposts, ruined portals, igloos, ocean ruins, fortresses) and in every landing platform's supply chest. Right-click to add the hidden world to your DHD's address list.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.redstone_transm: Sends the redstone signal going into it over one of 64 channels - any distance, any dimension (while its chunk is loaded). Right-click to pick the channel, sneak + right-click to go back. Its red light shows when it's sending.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.redstone_receiv: Gives out the strongest signal any transmitter is sending on its channel (1-64), to all sides and through the block it's on. Right-click to pick the channel, sneak + right-click to go back. Pair it with a Logic Controller, a Machine Status Display's comparator output or a lever across the base - or the Stargate DHD's redstone dialling, from anywhere.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.machine_status_: Right-click for a list of every machine within 24 blocks and what it's doing: Working, Idle, Blocked (it has items but isn't running - output full or something missing), No power, or Off (paused by redstone). Problems are listed first; filter by clicking the chips at the top. Its screen glows green when all is well, amber when something is blocked and red when something is out of power, and a comparator next to it gives the number of machines that need attention.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.digital_factory: The controller of a multiblock ore factory. Build Factory Cells onto it - touching it or each other, any shape, up to 16 - and every cell runs 4 operations at once (up to 64 per cycle; a cycle takes 5 seconds, faster with Speed upgrades). Modes: Smelt (furnace recipes), Crush (like the Pulverizer: 2 dust per ore), Wash (like the Ore Purifier: 3 dust per ore, 250 mB water each) and Ore to Ingots (washes, then smelts the dust: 3 ingots per ore). Nine input and nine output slots; 20 FE/t per operation smelting, 40 crushing, 60 washing and 80 for Ore to Ingots - the same as the separate machines. Water, power and items go into the controller or any Factory Port on the structure.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.factory_cell: Part of a Digital Factory: place it touching the controller or another cell (any shape). Each cell adds 4 operations at once, up to 16 cells (64 at once).
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.factory_port: Part of a Digital Factory: place it touching the controller or a cell. Pipes, cables and hoppers on a port reach the controller - items in go to the input slots, items out come from the output slots, and water and power flow in.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.guardian_altar: Found in the outposts on every planet. Sneak + right-click it to call the planet's guardian - an optional boss with 300 health, heavy armour and a boss bar (a Stray on Frost, a Husk on Dune, a Wither Skeleton on Inferno, a Ravager on Mycelia, an Evoker in the Void Reach and so on). Beat it for a Guardian Heart, Naquadah, diamonds, Mk II upgrades, an address and the planet's own material. Each altar calls one guardian, then goes dark.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.guardian_heart: Dropped by planet guardians. Not needed for anything - but it's a shortcut: with a Quantum Installer it makes a Naquadah Installer (no planet materials), and with four Speed or Energy Upgrades it makes four Mk II upgrades.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.lifebloom: A pink flower that grows only on Eden. Four of them make the Regeneration Module for the Quantum Suit.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.sunstone_ore: Found only on the Karoo, in stone and terracotta. Drops Sunstone.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.sunstone: A glowing orange stone from the Karoo that burns like 40 coal - 64,000 ticks in a Coal Generator or furnace.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.amber_ore: Found only in the Redwood, in stone. Drops Amber.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.amber: Hardened resin from the Redwood. Makes the Resistance Module for the Quantum Suit.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.witchroot: A gnarled root that grows only in the Murk. Makes the Antidote Module for the Quantum Suit.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.gravitite_ore: Found only on Titan, deep in its mountains. Needs a diamond pickaxe. Drops Gravitite.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.gravitite: A heavy violet crystal from Titan. Makes the Haste Module for the Quantum Suit.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.soul_crystal_or: Found only on Wraith, in soul sand, soul soil and netherrack. Drops Soul Crystals.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.soul_crystal: A cold blue crystal from Wraith. Makes the Fire Immunity Module for the Quantum Suit.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.umbral_ore: Found only in Umbra, in deepslate and stone. Needs a diamond pickaxe. Drops Umbral Shards.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.umbral_shard: A shard of solid darkness from Umbra. Makes the Stealth Module for the Quantum Suit.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.voidstone_ore: Found only in the Void Reach, in end stone. Needs a diamond pickaxe. Drops Void Shards.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.void_shard: A shard of the void. Eight around an Eye of Ender make a Void Pearl.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.void_pearl: An ender pearl that comes back: throw it as often as you like, with a 3 second wait between throws.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.regeneration_mo: Quantum Suit chestplate module: heals you over time while you're hurt (Regeneration I). 800 FE a second while healing.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.resistance_modu: Quantum Suit leggings module: Resistance I - a fifth off all damage. 200 FE a second.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.antidote_module: Quantum Suit helmet module: cures poison, wither, hunger, nausea, blindness, darkness, weakness and slowness as soon as they hit. 500 FE per cure.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.haste_module: Quantum Suit helmet module: Haste II - mine and swing faster. 200 FE a second.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.fire_immunity_m: Quantum Suit leggings module: fire and lava don't hurt you while it's charged. 300 FE a second while you're burning.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.stealth_module: Quantum Suit boots module: you turn invisible while you sneak. 200 FE a second while sneaking.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.sugar_cane_seed: One sugar cane makes two. Plant them like sugar cane: on sand, dirt or grass with water right beside that block (not on top of it) - or on Irrigated Sand under a Sprinkler, no water needed. The Crop Farmer plants them too.
tooltip.tieredpower.desc.irrigated_sand: Sand for greenhouses: sugar cane grows on it without a water channel, as long as a Sprinkler with water in it is overhead (within 4 blocks sideways and up to 8 blocks above). Water beside it works too, like normal sand, and cactus grows on it. It doesn't fall. Lay it where the farmland would go, in reach of the Crop Farmer, and the farmer plants Sugar Cane Seeds on it. 8 sand around a water bucket makes 8 (you get the bucket back).
